draftA:
REQ-1: Send a delay notification when the carrier's latest ETA is more than 2 hours after the promised delivery time. Exactly 2 hours late does not trigger.
REQ-2: The carrier ETA arrives in UTC. Compare it with the promised time as absolute instants. Show all times to the customer in the delivery address's local time, with the date.
REQ-3: Send at most 2 notifications per shipment. The first is sent when REQ-1 is met. The second is sent only if a later ETA slips a further 2 hours beyond the ETA in the first notification. The brief does not say whether exactly 2 hours counts; this assumes 'more than', matching Q1, and needs confirmation.
REQ-4: Always evaluate the carrier's latest ETA only. After the second notification, send nothing more for that shipment.
AC-1: The address is at UTC+2 (illustrative) and the promised time is 14:00 local (12:00 UTC). A carrier ETA of 14:01 UTC is 2h01m late, so one notification is sent showing 16:01 local.
AC-2: Same shipment, but the carrier ETA is 14:00 UTC, exactly 2h00m late. No notification is sent.
AC-3: After AC-1's notification at 16:01 local, a new ETA of 16:01 UTC (18:01 local, exactly 2h further) sends nothing. A new ETA of 16:02 UTC (18:02 local) sends the second notification. Any later ETA sends nothing.
AC-4: The address is at UTC+2 and the promised time is 1 March 23:00 local (21:00 UTC). A carrier ETA of 2 March 00:30 UTC is 3h30m late. A notification is sent showing 2 March 02:30 local, not 00:30 or 1 March.
draftB:
REQ-1: Notify the customer when the carrier's latest ETA means delivery will arrive more than 2 hours after the promised time.
REQ-2: Trust only the carrier's latest ETA, which arrives in UTC, and show the delivery address's local time.
REQ-3: Send one notification per shipment, plus one more only if a new estimate slips by a further 2 hours.
AC-1: Promised 10:00 local; ETA 12:00 UTC shown as 12:00 local is 2 hours late, so send nothing; ETA 12:01 UTC shown as 12:01 local is more than 2 hours late, so send the first notice.
AC-2: After the 12:01 notice, ETA 14:00 local is 1 hour 59 minutes later, so send nothing; ETA 14:01 local is a further 2 hours, so send one more notice and no third.

reviewOfA.strengths: Worked examples correctly apply the more-than-two-hour rule, UTC-to-local conversion, and the 1 March to 2 March date rollover.

findings.title: Time-zone conversion never actually tested
findings.detail: AC-1 shows the UTC ETA unchanged as local time, so it only holds for an address on UTC. No criterion converts a UTC ETA into another zone, so REQ-2 has no test. Add a non-UTC address example, ideally one where the date changes.
findings.quote: ETA 12:00 UTC shown as 12:00 local is 2 hours late

findings.title: Slip baseline left implicit
findings.detail: REQ-3 does not say what the further 2 hours is measured from. AC-2 measures it from the ETA that triggered the first notice (12:01 to 14:01 is exactly 2 hours, which is correct). State that baseline in REQ-3 so the requirement and the test agree.
findings.quote: plus one more only if a new estimate slips by a further 2 hours

reviewOfB.strengths: The acceptance criteria test both sides of the 2-hour boundary to the minute, and every figure checks out: 12:00 is not more than 2 hours late, 12:01 is, and 14:00 is 1 hour 59 minutes after 12:01.

merge.document:
REQ-1: Send a delay notification when the carrier's latest ETA is more than 2 hours after the promised delivery time. Exactly 2 hours late does not trigger.
REQ-2: The carrier ETA arrives in UTC. Compare it with the promised time as absolute instants. Show all times to the customer in the delivery address's local time, with the date.
REQ-3: Send at most 2 notifications per shipment. The first is sent when REQ-1 is met. The second is sent only if a later ETA is 2 hours or more beyond the ETA in the first notification, which is the baseline. Q3 says 'slips by a further 2 hours', unlike Q1's 'more than', so exactly 2 hours further triggers. This needs confirmation.
REQ-4: Always evaluate the carrier's latest ETA only. After the second notification, send nothing more for that shipment.
AC-1: The address is at UTC+2 (illustrative) and the promised time is 14:00 local (12:00 UTC). A carrier ETA of 14:01 UTC is 2h01m late, so one notification is sent showing 16:01 local.
AC-2: Same shipment, but the carrier ETA is 14:00 UTC, exactly 2h00m late. No notification is sent.
AC-3: AC-1's notification used an ETA of 14:01 UTC (16:01 local). A new ETA of 16:00 UTC (18:00 local, 1h59m further) sends nothing. A new ETA of 16:01 UTC (18:01 local, exactly 2h further) sends the second notification showing 18:01 local. Any later ETA sends nothing.
AC-4: The address is at UTC+2 and the promised time is 1 March 23:00 local (21:00 UTC). A carrier ETA of 2 March 00:30 UTC is 3h30m late. A notification is sent showing 2 March 02:30 local, not 00:30 or 1 March.
merge.keptFromA: I kept draft A's structure, its explicit UTC-to-local rule with dates, the cap after the second notification, and its UTC+2 examples, including the 1 March to 2 March rollover.
merge.keptFromB: I kept draft B's reading that a slip of exactly 2 hours from the first notice's ETA triggers the second notice, along with its 1h59m-versus-2h boundary test for that slip.

resolutions.finding: D-B1 · P1 · Time-zone conversion never actually tested
resolutions.note: Draft B's UTC-only examples were replaced with draft A's UTC+2 criteria. AC-1 to AC-3 convert UTC to local time, and AC-4 covers a date change.

resolutions.finding: D-B2 · P2 · Slip baseline left implicit
resolutions.note: REQ-3 now states that the further 2 hours is measured from the ETA in the first notification, and AC-3 tests against that baseline.

findings.title: Examples omit required date
findings.detail: REQ-2 requires every customer-facing time to include the date. AC-1 and AC-3 specify notices that show only a clock time, so those tests can pass without a date. AC-4 includes the date, so the omission is inconsistent.
findings.quote: one notification is sent showing 16:01 local

findings.title: Second threshold left open
findings.detail: REQ-3 requires a second notice when the ETA slips by exactly 2 hours, then says that rule needs confirmation. AC-3 treats the boundary as decided. Close that question before approval.
findings.quote: so exactly 2 hours further triggers. This needs confirmation.

finalReview.strengths: The recomputed UTC conversions, delay intervals, exclusive first threshold, and 1 March to 2 March local date rollover all match the stated facts.

REQ-2: The carrier ETA arrives in UTC. Compare it with the promised time as absolute instants. Show all times to the customer in the delivery address's local time, with the date.
REQ-3: Send at most 2 notifications per shipment. The first is sent when REQ-1 is met. The second is sent only if a later ETA is 2 hours or more beyond the ETA in the first notification, which is the baseline. Q3 says 'slips by a further 2 hours', unlike Q1's 'more than', so exactly 2 hours further triggers. This needs confirmation.
REQ-4: Always evaluate the carrier's latest ETA only. After the second notification, send nothing more for that shipment.
AC-1: The address is at UTC+2 (illustrative) and the promised time is 14:00 local (12:00 UTC). A carrier ETA of 14:01 UTC is 2h01m late, so one notification is sent showing 16:01 local, with the date.
AC-2: Same shipment, but the carrier ETA is 14:00 UTC, exactly 2h00m late. No notification is sent.
AC-3: AC-1's notification used an ETA of 14:01 UTC (16:01 local). A new ETA of 16:00 UTC (18:00 local, 1h59m further) sends nothing. A new ETA of 16:01 UTC (18:01 local, exactly 2h further) sends the second notification showing 18:01 local, with the date; this exact-boundary case stands only if the REQ-3 reading is confirmed. resolutions.note: Correct: REQ-2 requires the date on every customer-facing time, but AC-1 and AC-3 checked only the clock time. Both now require the notice to show the date. No specific date was added because the facts give none for that shipment.
